title: Module derived restriction on injective section complexes
statement:
Let $u:T'\to T$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring. Use sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves $\Lambda_T,\Lambda_{T'}$ on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ be the exact module inverse-image adjunction of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and compute derived direct image and derived sections within these module categories [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. Write $Q_T,Q_{T'},Q_\Lambda$ for localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $I,J$ be bounded-below complexes of injective module sheaves on $T,T'$ respectively [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $a:u^{-1}I\to J$ be any module-linear chain map. Let $e_{u,I}:\Gamma(T,I)\to\Gamma(T',u^{-1}I)$ be the degreewise adjunction-unit section map, using $\Gamma(T,u_*F)=\Gamma(T',F)$. Let $\alpha_I:Q_\Lambda\Gamma(T,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(T,Q_TI)$ and $\alpha_J:Q_\Lambda\Gamma(T',J)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(T',Q_{T'}J)$ be the canonical resolution comparisons. Identify $u^{-1}(Q_TI)$ with $Q_{T'}(u^{-1}I)$ by exactness, and define $\mathrm{res}_u:R\Gamma(T,Q_TI)\to R\Gamma(T',Q_{T'}u^{-1}I)$ as $R\Gamma$ of the derived adjunction unit followed by the canonical module Leray comparison $R\Gamma(T,Ru_*N)\cong R\Gamma(T',N)$. Then the following is an equality in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$:
$$R\Gamma(T',Q_{T'}a)\circ\mathrm{res}_u=\alpha_J\circ Q_\Lambda\bigl(\Gamma(T',a)\circ e_{u,I}\bigr)\circ\alpha_I^{-1}.$$
No quasi-isomorphism condition on $a$ and no finiteness condition on $u$ or $\Lambda$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(T'_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. These are the module categories throughout the argument. They have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The exact adjunction of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] imply that $u_*J$ is termwise injective; it remains bounded below. Thus $I,J,u_*J$ are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Write $\delta_L:Q_Tu_*L\to Ru_*Q_{T'}L$ for the direct-image comparison and $\alpha^S_L:Q_\Lambda\Gamma(S,L)\to R\Gamma(S,Q_SL)$ for the sections comparison. They are natural and invertible on bounded-below injective complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. These are also the comparisons for the unbounded module-valued sections in [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]: that definition uses the same K-injective complexes, and [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] computes morphisms by the same homotopy classes. Its resolution-existence hypothesis holds by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist].

Let $\eta_I:I\to u_*u^{-1}I$ be the degreewise ordinary unit, and put $t=u_*a\circ\eta_I:I\to u_*J$. The termwise adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], applied to the module adjunction of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], says precisely that $t$ is a chain map and is the ordinary homotopy-category transpose of $a$. At the terminal object $T$, the direct-image formula in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $(u_*a)^n(T)=a^n(T')$. By the definition of $e_{u,I}$ this proves, in each degree and hence as chain maps of $\Lambda$-modules,
$$\Gamma(T,t)=\Gamma(T',a)\circ e_{u,I}.$$
The differentials commute because $\eta$ is natural; all scalar actions are retained by the module adjunction.

For the specified $a$, calculate its derived transpose directly. Exactness gives $D(u^{-1})(Q_TI)=Q_{T'}u^{-1}I$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Since $J$ and $u_*J$ are K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(Q_{T'}u^{-1}I,Q_{T'}J)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal B)}(u^{-1}I,J)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(I,u_*J)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(Q_TI,Q_Tu_*J).$$
This sends $Q_{T'}a$ to $Q_Tt$. The bijections are natural: the middle one is natural by the termwise adjunction, and the outer ones are the localization bijections; target derived maps are represented by homotopy classes between injective representatives. Postcomposing with $\delta_J$ gives the Hom bijection for the canonical derived adjunction, namely the localization of the ordinary adjunction computed on injective targets. By the unit formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], its transpose is also $Ru_*(Q_{T'}a)\circ\eta^D_{Q_TI}$. Consequently
$$Ru_*(Q_{T'}a)\circ\eta^D_{Q_TI}=\delta_J\circ Q_Tt.$$
This calculation takes place in module categories and does not require $a$ to be a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text:
Normalize the Leray map on the same module models. For a bounded-below derived $\mathcal B$-object $N$, choose an injective representative $Q_{T'}L\cong N$ using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Then $Ru_*N$ is represented by $u_*L$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and $u_*L$ is a bounded-below injective complex by Step 1. Both successive derived functors can therefore be evaluated without a further replacement. The equality of module complexes $\Gamma(T,u_*L)=\Gamma(T',L)$ defines the canonical Leray comparison $\lambda_N$. More explicitly, for $N=Q_{T'}J$ this normalization reads
$$\lambda_{Q_{T'}J}\circ R\Gamma(T,\delta_J)\circ\alpha^T_{u_*J}=\alpha_J.$$
To check naturality and independence of $L$, lift a derived morphism to a homotopy class between the chosen injective representatives using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Applying $u_*$ and then $\Gamma(T,-)$ gives literally the same map as $\Gamma(T',-)$, by the direct-image formula; comparisons for different choices are homotopy equivalences. Thus the equation is compatible with all changes of representatives. It is the composition-of-derived-functors comparison of Stacks 08J6/015M: deriving $\Gamma(T,u_*(-))=\Gamma(T',-)$ on these models gives exactly this identity, and the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] fixes its normalization. In particular it supplies naturality at $Q_{T'}a$.

proof.text:
By the definition of $\mathrm{res}_u$, naturality of $\lambda$ at $Q_{T'}a$, and Step 3, the left side of the required identity is
$$\lambda_{Q_{T'}J}\circ R\Gamma\bigl(T,Ru_*(Q_{T'}a)\circ\eta^D_{Q_TI}\bigr)
=\lambda_{Q_{T'}J}\circ R\Gamma(T,\delta_J)\circ R\Gamma(T,Q_Tt).$$
Naturality of the sections comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] at $t:I\to u_*J$ gives
$$R\Gamma(T,Q_Tt)\circ\alpha_I=\alpha^T_{u_*J}\circ Q_\Lambda\Gamma(T,t).$$
Substituting this and the normalization in Step 4 reduces the left side to $\alpha_J\circ Q_\Lambda\Gamma(T,t)\circ\alpha_I^{-1}$. Step 2 replaces $\Gamma(T,t)$ by $\Gamma(T',a)\circ e_{u,I}$, proving the displayed formula in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$. These substitutions use only functoriality and invertibility of the stated resolution comparisons. No inverse to $a$, finite-type hypothesis on $u$, or finiteness assumption on $\Lambda$ has been used.
